page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.small is an entry-level virtual server instance belonging to the shared resource family. It is provisioned with 1 shared vCPU backed by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The single execution thread has access to 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 33 MB L3 cache pool. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance includes no local storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent data, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps without bundled GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints of a single shared core on older hardware. Across standard synthetic evaluations, the processor registers 1086.18 in single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 871.0 and multi-core score of 877.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 75.4 GB/sec for small cached blocks but drops to 8.16 GB/sec read and 7.36 GB/sec write on 256 MB uncached transfers. Application-level metrics demonstrate 1.23 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 0.93 GB/sec throughput in static web serving.

From an infrastructure perspective, ecs.e4.small offers a low-cost profile tailored for workloads that require modest memory allocations without sustained compute throughput. Because the shared vCPU shares host execution pipelines and has baseline network bandwidth rated at 0 Gbps, performance will exhibit variability under high contention. The instance is suited for lightweight background utilities, small staging environments, internal development testing, and low-volume web serving or proxying tasks that can tolerate shared-tier throughput limits.
